qs.q: A 13‑year‑old boy presents with sudden severe right testicular pain after swimming. Color Doppler ultrasound is obtained. Which Doppler finding most strongly supports testicular torsion rather than epididymitis?
o: Presence of a simple hydrocele fluid rim surrounding the testis
Observation of increased intratesticular arterial blood flow
Maintenance of a normal caliber of the pampiniform plexus
Demonstration of absent or reduced intratesticular arterial flow
qs.e: Absent or reduced intratesticular arterial flow indicates arterial compromise typical of torsion, whereas epididymitis usually shows hyperemia. Increased arterial flow (option B) reflects inflammation, not torsion.
